# STEMpathi: Hands-on Math

> A hands-on math app for children aged 5 to 11 (from first counting at Pre-K–K to equations at grades 5–7). Children move cubes, tens and hundreds on a balance scale to learn counting, place value and equations. Works fully offline. No ads, no account, no analytics, no tracking SDKs, and no backend: the app sends nothing to the makers; progress stays on the device. Free to download; today every lesson is free and there are no in-app purchases. Android, in a Google Play test; not yet on iPhone or iPad. Made by Sripathi.One.

Key facts (true as of 2026-11-15):
- Method: concrete pieces first, then pictures, then numbers (Bruner's enactive–iconic–symbolic modes); a balance scale for the meaning of the equal sign; negative numbers as balloons that pull a pan up; islands in learning order, informed by the learning-trajectories approach (Clements & Sarama).
- Islands: Counting Shore (Pre-K–K), Make-Ten Reef (K–1), Tens Harbour (grades 1–2), Hundreds Peaks (grades 2–3), Sharing Bridge (grades 3–4), Unknowns Summit (grades 5–7).
- Standards: practises US Common Core topics from K.CC to 6.EE (the makers' own alignment, not an endorsement).
- Calm design: no timers to beat, no points race, a hint from the guide Avi when a child is stuck, calm motion and night mode.
- Not claimed: no study of learning outcomes has been run; no ratings or awards.
